diagram:
flowchart TD
  SCHED["⏰ pg_cron per market\nUS 20:15 UTC · India 11:15 UTC · maxDuration 120s"] --> OPEN["📋 Fetch open paper_positions\nno closed_at column — existence = open"]
  OPEN --> PRICE["💲 Per-position prices\nMassive prev-agg · India via Yahoo .NS"]
  PRICE --> TRAIL["📈 Trailing stop\nanchored to each position's own stop distance"]
  TRAIL --> EXITS{"🚪 Exit checks"}
  EXITS -->|"stop breached"| CLOSE["✅ execute_paper_exit RPC\nrealized P&L + outcome → RAG"]
  EXITS -->|"target hit"| PARTIAL["½ Partial target\nsell half · stop → breakeven"]
  EXITS -->|"fresh holding score below exit threshold"| SCOREEXIT["📉 score_reassess_exit\ndeterministic, hysteresis-gated"]
  EXITS -->|"horizon reached"| TIME["⏳ Time stop\nmandate/genome horizon · grandfathered"]
  EXITS -->|"none"| HOLD["⏳ Hold"]
  PARTIAL --> CLOSE
  SCOREEXIT --> CLOSE
  TIME --> CLOSE
  CLOSE --> NAV["🏦 NAV invariant + cash-ledger drift alert"]
  NAV --> BREAKER["🔴 Drawdown circuit breaker\nauto-pauses the market"]
  SCHED -.-> ERRLOG["🚨 logMonitorError\nwrites agent_runs status='error'"]

SCHED.label: pg_cron per market
SCHED.description: TWO per-market pg_cron jobs: US 15 20 * * 1-5 (16:15 ET, post-close) and India 15 11 * * 1-5 (16:45 IST). maxDuration = 120s with force-dynamic. Deterministic — a Flow, not an LLM.
SCHED.addReason: Post-close is when the day's exits are evaluated.
SCHED.changeReason: US time was right but the India job was undrawn, the mechanism is pg_cron, and maxDuration=120 was never recorded.

OPEN.label: Fetch open positions
OPEN.description: Loads all rows from paper_positions. There is no closed_at column on this table — existence in it IS the open state; exits delete the row via RPC.
OPEN.addReason: Only open positions can be exited.
OPEN.changeReason: Verified accurate; amended only to record that openness is represented by row existence, which the code documents explicitly and which a reader would otherwise expect to be a status column.

PRICE.label: Current prices
PRICE.description: Fetched PER POSITION via Promise.allSettled — not batched. US uses the Massive previous-aggregate endpoint; India uses fetchIndiaQuote (Yahoo .NS). There is NO Polygon fallback.
PRICE.changeReason: Both claims false: it is per-position rather than batched, and the Polygon fallback does not exist. India's separate quote path was undrawn.

TRAIL.label: Trailing stop
TRAIL.description: The stop rises with the new high and never falls — but the trail distance is POSITION-SPECIFIC, derived from that position's own initial_stop_loss / avg_cost ratio (clamped 0.5-0.99). The 0.93 / 7% figure is only the fallback used when initial_stop_loss is null; the code names it as 'not a hardcoded 7%'.
TRAIL.addReason: Let winners run while protecting profit.
TRAIL.changeReason: The monotonic-ratchet property is accurate and kept; the implied universal 7% trail is not — the distance is per-position.

EXITS.label: Exit checks
EXITS.description: Five exit families run here, where the diagram drew two: stop breach, partial target, deterministic score-decay / direction-flip, time stop, and hedge_exit for position_role='hedge' positions. A score-freshness hold suppresses score-based exits on stale scores; protective stop exits are never suppressed.
EXITS.addReason: The old TARGET/FLAG pair could not express the exit surface that actually ships.

PARTIAL.label: Partial target
PARTIAL.description: Hitting the price target no longer closes the position outright: it sells floor(qty/2) as exit_reason='partial_target' and moves the stop to breakeven, letting the remainder run. A full 'target_hit' close only happens when qty is 1.
PARTIAL.addReason: Shipped undrawn, and it materially changes what 'target hit' means — the diagram implied a full exit.

SCOREEXIT.label: score_reassess_exit
SCOREEXIT.description: The current thesis-break exit is deterministic and daily: a position closes only when its fresh holding-path score decays below the hysteresis-gated exit threshold. The stored short direction is derived from score and cannot bypass hysteresis. No LLM is involved. 'llm_exit' is honoured only to drain legacy rows.
SCOREEXIT.addReason: Replaces the FLAG node, which credited exits to a learner-set LLM flag that no longer governs them.
SCOREEXIT.changeReason: Holding provenance and the exit threshold now both gate score exits.

TIME.label: Time stop
TIME.description: Positions held past the mandate/genome hold horizon are exited, with grandfathering so a mandate change cannot retroactively force-close positions opened under the old horizon.
TIME.addReason: An entire exit family the diagram never mentioned.

CLOSE.label: Close + write outcome
CLOSE.description: Closes via the execute_paper_exit RPC (transactional), records realized P&L and outcome — which becomes the LearnerAgent's ground truth — and indexes the closed trade into RAG. Hedge exits additionally reconcile through complete_paper_hedge_exit.
CLOSE.changeReason: Verified accurate; amended to name the RPC (the close is transactional, not a bare update) and the RAG indexing that follows it.

NAV.label: NAV + ledger checks
NAV.description: After exits: a NAV invariant check, a cash-ledger drift alert, benchmark/alpha sync, and a health alert if the NAV write fails — so a silently wrong NAV surfaces instead of compounding.
NAV.addReason: Undrawn post-exit accounting; these are the checks that make the P&L trustworthy.

BREAKER.label: Drawdown breaker
BREAKER.description: A NAV drawdown breach auto-PAUSES that market — the one place in this flow that changes system state beyond a position. Per-market, so a US breach cannot pause India.
BREAKER.addReason: A control that halts trading was completely absent from the diagram of the flow that trips it.

ERRLOG.label: Error logging
ERRLOG.description: On failure the route writes an agent_runs row with status='error' rather than dying silently, so the stale-run check sees an errored run instead of an absence. Absence and failure look identical to a monitor; this makes them different.
ERRLOG.addReason: A monitor that fails silently is worse than no monitor — this path is why it does not.

HOLD.label: Hold
HOLD.description: No exit condition met — position carries to the next session.

history.label: Holding provenance and hysteresis enforced
history.reason: Only signals produced on the holding path can participate in reassessment, and their deterministic short direction cannot bypass the lower exit threshold. Candidate signals never close an owned position.

history.label: llm_exit no longer governs exits — replaced by deterministic score_reassess_exit
history.reason: The node claimed exits are flagged by the LearnerAgent when a thesis breaks, with the monitor executing the close — 'clean separation of concerns'. That separation no longer exists, and neither does the flagger. The LLM-discretion exit path was REMOVED on 2026-07-15; the current thesis-break exit is deterministic and daily (score decayed below a hysteresis-gated threshold, or direction flipped) and is flagged score_reassess_exit. 'llm_exit' survives in the code only to drain legacy rows flagged before that removal — honoured for back-compat, never newly written. This was not a harmless stale label: it told the reader that a weekly LLM was watching their open positions for broken theses. Nothing is. What actually protects a decayed position is a daily deterministic check the diagram never drew, now SCOREEXIT. Corroborating evidence on the same page: the LearnerAgent stopped force-closing positions on a timer entirely — exits are now fully owned by this flow.

history.label: Not batched, and the Polygon fallback does not exist
history.reason: 'Batch-fetches current prices via the Massive API (Polygon fallback)' is wrong twice. Prices are fetched PER POSITION via Promise.allSettled against the Massive previous-aggregate endpoint — there is no batch call — and there is no Polygon fallback anywhere in the route. The fallback claim is the more dangerous of the two: it asserts a redundancy this flow does not have, so a Massive outage means the US exit checks run on whatever prices resolved, with no second source. India was undrawn entirely and uses a different path (fetchIndiaQuote / Yahoo .NS). Reported as a documentation correction only; whether to BUILD the fallback the diagram promised is a code decision for the owner.

history.label: Trail distance is per-position, not a universal 7%
history.reason: The ratchet property — stop rises with the high, never falls — is verified accurate and kept. The distance was not: the trail is anchored to each position's OWN initial_stop_loss / avg_cost ratio (clamped 0.5-0.99), so a name entered on a tight stop trails tight and one entered wide trails wide. 0.93 is only the fallback for positions with a null initial_stop_loss, and the code explicitly annotates itself 'not a hardcoded 7%'. The old diagram's max(original_stop_loss, highest_price × 0.93) would tell a reader every position trails at 7%, which would misprice the expected drawdown of every position in the book.

history.label: Five exit families, where the diagram drew two (+ PARTIAL, SCOREEXIT, TIME)
history.reason: The old TARGET/FLAG pair described a two-exit system (target-or-stop, plus the defunct llm_exit). Five families actually run: stop breach; PARTIAL target; deterministic score-decay / direction-flip; TIME stop against the mandate/genome hold horizon with grandfathering so a mandate change cannot retroactively force-close older positions; and hedge_exit for position_role='hedge' rows, reconciled via complete_paper_hedge_exit. PARTIAL is the correction most likely to surprise: hitting the price target no longer closes the position — it sells floor(qty/2), moves the stop to breakeven, and lets the rest run, with a full target_hit close only when qty is 1. Anyone reconciling their book against this diagram would have expected flat positions where half-positions exist. Also recorded the score-freshness hold, which suppresses score-based exits on stale scores but deliberately never suppresses a protective stop.

history.label: NAV drawdown circuit breaker auto-pauses the market — undrawn
history.reason: A control that HALTS TRADING for a whole market was missing from the diagram of the flow that trips it. On a NAV drawdown breach the route calls setMarketPaused for that market, which is the only place in this flow where state beyond an individual position changes. Per-market, so a US breach cannot pause India. Drawn with NAV (invariant check, cash-ledger drift alert, benchmark/alpha sync, NAV-write-failure health alert) because the breaker is only as trustworthy as the NAV it reads, and those checks are what make that NAV trustworthy.

history.label: logMonitorError writes an errored agent_runs row instead of failing silently
history.reason: Undrawn and load-bearing for a monitor specifically: absence and failure are indistinguishable to anything watching a scheduled job. On failure the route writes an agent_runs row with status='error' so the stale-run check sees an ERRORED run rather than silence, which is the difference between 'the monitor is broken' and 'nothing needed doing today' — on a flow whose job is closing losing positions, that distinction is the whole safety story. Drawn as a dotted edge off SCHED because it is a cross-cutting failure path, not a step. Noted for contrast during this audit: paper-trade has NO maxDuration at all, though it does finalize a zombie run in its catch. Not fixed — code change, and out of scope for a documentation task.

history.label: Two per-market pg_cron jobs; US time verified, India was undrawn; maxDuration 120s
history.reason: The US claim '4:15 PM post-close' is verified ACCURATE (pg_cron 15 20 * * 1-5 = 16:15 ET) and its reasoning kept. Corrections: the mechanism is Supabase pg_cron rather than the implied Windows scheduler, a SECOND India job exists (15 11 * * 1-5, 16:45 IST) that the single-schedule diagram hid, and maxDuration = 120 with force-dynamic was never recorded — relevant because this flow's per-position price fetches scale with the size of the book, so the ceiling is a real constraint rather than boilerplate. 'Deterministic — a Flow, not an LLM' verified accurate and kept verbatim.

history.label: Verified accurate — amended to name the RPC and the RAG indexing
history.reason: 'Closes the position, records realized P&L and outcome — which becomes the LearnerAgent's ground truth' is TRUE and the node is materially unchanged; no churn invented. Amended on two points found while verifying: the close goes through the execute_paper_exit RPC (transactional, not a bare update — which is why a partial fill and a cash-ledger update cannot diverge), and the closed trade is indexed into RAG afterwards, feeding the learner's semantic recall. Hedge exits additionally reconcile via complete_paper_hedge_exit. Same for OPEN: verified accurate, amended only to record that paper_positions has no closed_at column, so row existence IS the open state and exits delete the row — a reader expecting a status filter would write a query that silently returns nothing.
